_note: Images the fetch mirrored that are not the badge they are filed under. Keyed by
SHA-256 of the bytes, because the same wrong image comes back byte-identical on every
re-run and its filename says nothing about what is inside it.
`sha256` is for images that are never anybody's badge. Either Wikipedia has no free
crest and its infobox holds a generic placeholder tile, or `resolve_title` lands on
the article about the PLACE instead of the club - 'Burgos' the city, 'Bahia' the
state - and the lead photograph is a skyline, a cathedral or a stadium. Both are worse
than nothing: the game draws no badge for a club without a crest so that the name
carries the row, and a photograph in that slot takes the decision away from it.
`misfiled` is for the other kind, and it is why this file is not just a list of
digests. A real mark can be the right image somewhere and the wrong one here: Club
Municipal Limeno mirrored the El Salvador Primera Division logo, which is byte-for-byte
the file the Primera Division itself correctly uses. Rejecting those bytes everywhere
would take the league's own mark away from it, so these are keyed by bucket and slug
AND digest - a later fetch that finds a different image for the same slug is kept.
Curated by eye. `scripts/audit-football-crests.py` finds the candidates - a photograph
has no flat region and a badge is nothing but flat regions - but only a person can say
whether a logo is the RIGHT logo, which is how the entry under `misfiled` got here.
Read by scripts/fetch-football-crests.py, which refuses to write these, and by
scripts/build-trayectoria-world.mjs, which skips them if an older mirror already has
them on disk. See `Crest` in src/games/sports/trayectoria/index.jsx for what the game
does with the resulting null.
